transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-06
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Huang (Redwood CSM), Marco Rivera (Redwood SE), Dr. Aisha Khan (Head of Data, Nova Clinic), Tom Reynolds (VP Eng, Nova Clinic), Maya Lopez (Security Lead), Diego Alvarez (SRE)

Summary (auto):
Kickoff for Nova Clinic onboarding to Redwood Inference. Covering implementation plan, infra needs (VPC, firewall, KMS), pilot goals, initial benchmark, timeline, and weekly sync cadence. Action items captured.

Topics:
- Project goals & success criteria
- Hosting mode: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC)
- Security: SOC2, SAML, KMS, audit logs
- Network and infra requirements (egress, ports, IP allowlist)
- Benchmarks and pilot plan
- Rollout and monitoring (Console, cost breakdown)

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate it. I'm Samir, AE on the account, Leah and Marco are with me from Customer Success and Solutions. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Dr. Aisha: Good, thanks. Excited to get started.
[00:15] Tom: Yep, thanks for organizing. We've been waiting to get this moving.
[00:22] Samir: Awesome. Quick agenda — we want to validate success criteria, decide hosting mode, get infra requirements, cover security docs, and lock a timeline for the two-week pilot. Sounds ok?
[00:35] Maya: That works. For us security is the blocker so we need SOC two, SAML, and KMS details early.
[00:42] Leah: Totally understood. We'll share our SOC2 and encryption whitepaper today and Samir will follow up with the addendum.
[00:50] Marco: On the technical side I'll need a small test dataset and access to a staging environment or IP allowlist to run the initial perf tests. We typically run sample throughput and latency tests with an input profile you provide.
[01:05] Diego: One thing — our infra team is picky about egress policies and we use strict firewall rules. We'll need exact port lists and any fixed IPs.
[01:12] Samir: Absolutely. We'll provide a network guide. For the initial pilot we can use Redwood Dedicated or Private VPC. Quick question for you Tom/Aisha — is data residency or air-gap a hard requirement or is VPC sufficient?
[01:29] Tom: For now VPC in our cloud region is fine, not air-gapped. But we do want customer-managed keys — HSM or KMS integration.
[01:38] Leah: Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM and audit logs; Dedicated also can be configured with KMS depending on the install. We'll attach the KMS integration doc.
[01:45] Dr. Aisha: Great. Our success criteria: 1) 95th latency under 250ms for single-turn prompts at 512 tokens, 2) monthly cost projection within budget (we have a target $X/token approximate), and 3) no PII retained beyond session — need auditability.
[02:05] Marco: Ok good. We'll aim to reproduce that with our benchmark. Quick note — depending on batching and KV cache behavior, latency can vary; we'll tune batching thresholds and cache policies to meet the SLO.
[02:22] Samir: Also wanted to call out model selection — we can start with a low-cost open model and then optionally switch to a faster quantized variant on Dedicated. That lets us measure quality vs cost tradeoffs.
[02:36] Tom: That sounds right. We do care about quality though — hallucination rate on clinical notes is a no-go. We'll need evals with your regression monitoring.
[02:46] Leah: We have a Redwood Optimize suggestion pack and eval hooks we can run against your prompt sets. We'll onboard that into the pipeline.
[02:55] Maya: On compliance — can you confirm retention controls and audit logs retention period? Our policy is 7 years for certain logs.
[03:03] Samir: We'll include retention controls in the security addendum; typical console retention is shorter but with enterprise add-on we can configure longer retention or ship logs to your SIEM.
[03:15] Diego: Can you push logs to our S3 bucket or Splunk?
[03:18] Marco: Yes, we support log export to S3 and Splunk. There may be setup steps for IAM roles; we'll include those in the infra guide.
[03:28] [crosstalk]
[03:35] Dr. Aisha: Walk us through the pilot steps end-to-end please — what should we expect week by week?
[03:42] Leah: Sure. Week 0 (this week) — access and network validation, share runbook. Week 1 — run baseline benchmark and initial quality evals. Week 2 — optimize config (batching, quantization), review results, and decide on next step (scale or dedicated rollout). We'll run a two-week pilot and produce a final recommendations doc.
[04:02] Samir: And pricing — for the pilot we can grant a short trial credit for Dedicated capacity; I'll put numbers in the follow-up.
[04:10] Tom: Will the trial be on our VPC or your hosted infra?
[04:14] Samir: It can be on Redwood Dedicated in your VPC tenant or on Redwood Private depending on the contract; for speed we usually spin a Dedicated instance in your cloud account using our deployment templates.
[04:26] Maya: What's the expected downtime for bringing up Dedicated?
[04:29] Marco: Typically a few hours for a basic Dedicated pool; if there are extra networking approvals it could take longer. We have Terraform templates to automate most of it.
[04:40] Diego: Ok good to know. We'll try to provision a dev VPC to test.
[04:45] [00:04:50] Samir: Quick note — sometimes the transcript says KV cache as K V, sorry for shorthand; it's the Key-Value cache for prompt prefixes. Also some names might get mangled in this auto transcript.
[04:58] Dr. Aisha: Understood. For the benchmark data we'll send a small synthetic dataset — about 2k prompts — that mimic our EMR notes. Any redactions recommended?
[05:08] Marco: Redact PHI where possible. We can also run on anonymized data. The benchmark script supports CSV inputs and returns latency and p99 metrics and token cost breakouts.
[05:22] Tom: On monitoring — what do we get out of the box in the Redwood Console?
[05:27] Leah: You get per-route latency/cost breakdowns, token counts, error rates, and an eval dashboard for regression alerts. We also provide tracing hooks for request-level debugging.
[05:40] Maya: Does the console have RBAC and SSO? We need SAML integration and role-based admin controls.
[05:46] Samir: Yes SSO via SAML, SCIM provisioning and RBAC are supported in Private and Dedicated. We'll pass the SSO integration guide.
[05:58] Dr. Aisha: Good. Any network changes required for SSO?
[06:02] Marco: Usually inbound from your IdP is not needed; it's an outbound flow. We'll document specifics.
[06:10] [06:10] Tom: About cost — can you provide unit economics for tokens for the models you plan to test? We need a sheet to plug our expected volume.
[06:19] Samir: I'll attach a pricing spreadsheet with expected per-token and per-embedding numbers plus Dedicated commit models. That will be in the follow-up.
[06:28] Diego: For the pilot we want a fake traffic profile — can you simulate bursts?
[06:33] Marco: Yes, our benchmark tool can simulate burst patterns and steady state. We'll run a couple of scenarios and surface tail latency and throughput.
[06:42] Maya: If we do Dedicated, what are the security boundaries? Is data shared across tenants?
[06:49] Leah: Dedicated capacity is isolated to your account; there's no shared storage for model KV cache. Private deployments give you full control over networking and keys. We'll include an architecture diagram.
[07:00] Dr. Aisha: Great. Any recommended quantization strategies for clinical prompts? We care about hallucination.
[07:06] Marco: We generally start with 8-bit quantized models with validation against your eval set; if quality drops we back off to higher precision or use a different model family. We'll show side-by-side QA metrics.
[07:19] Samir: Ok want to circle back to timeline and owners before we close — Leah, you'll coordinate weekly cadence. Marco will own the bench runs. Samir will send docs/pricing. Customers — Maya and Diego will provision network and security contacts and Aisha/Tom will provide the eval prompts.
[07:40] Maya: Yes that's fine. I'll loop in our network team once we have the list of required ports.
[07:45] Diego: I'll create a dev VPC and email the contact info.
[07:49] Dr. Aisha: We'll prepare and scrub a 2k prompt sample by EOD Friday.
[07:55] Samir: Perfect. Any other blockers or questions?
[07:59] Tom: One ask — can you include a clear rollback plan if the pilot shows regressions? We need failover to our old pipeline.
[08:08] Marco: Yes, we include fallback policies and can keep a canary routing split so traffic can be directed away automatically. We'll document the rollback steps.
[08:18] [08:18] Samir: Ok quick recap of next steps: Samir to send onboarding pack and pricing; Marco to run benchmarks after network is provisioned; Maya/Diego to provide network details and test IPs; Leah to set weekly sync. We'll target first benchmark by 2025-11-14.
[08:36] Maya: Sounds good.
[08:38] Leah: I'll create the calendar invite for Thursdays 10am PT starting 2025-11-13.
[08:44] Samir: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs.
[08:47] Dr. Aisha: Thanks, talk soon.
[08:49] Tom: Thanks all.
[08:51] [END]
